newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen mixed to down, peso stable.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen mixed to down, peso stable.

text.p: Traders saw most share prices sagging at Monday's open on profit-taking carried over from the previous session and amid sporadic bargain-hunting ahead of second quarter earnings reports.
"There's still a lot of profits to be taken, but some will be positioning ahead of Q2 reports," a desk trader said.
Technical analysts situated support for the leading IPC index at 4,800 points, down from Friday's close of 4,821.62.
Traders expected the peso to open stable as most banks had already squared their books and were not moving in the absence any fresh economic or political news, they said.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8450/7.8650 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.8550/7.8590 per dollar, compared to Friday's close of 7.8540/7.8570.
Overnight Cetes rates were seen opening slightly up from Friday's 19.00 percent close on a surplus of paper, while some dealers could switch to dollars due to current peso strength.
